podcast.title: Claimant to Frankie Lymon's Estate
podcast.body: Zola Taylor was one of three women who claimed to be Frankie Lymon's legitimate widow in the 1980s, alleging a bigamous marriage a year after his first, though she could not provide any evidence for this claim. "One was Zola Taylor, who Lyman supposedly married Bigamously a year after his first marriage, but who couldn't produce any evidence of this."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Completing Book Ram's Ideal Lineup
podcast.body: Zola Taylor was specifically chosen by Book Ram to join The Platters. Her addition completed Ram's vision for the group's vocal sound, which was a blend of four men and one woman, inspired by earlier groups like The Quintones and The Modernaires. "With Zola in the group, Ram's ideal vocal sound was almost complete."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Replaced in The Platters
podcast.body: Sandra Doyle, who briefly joined The Teenagers, later replaced Zola Taylor as a member of The Platters. "who would later be Zola Taylor's replacement in the Platters."

podcast.title: Solo Artist Before The Platters
podcast.body: Before joining The Platters, Zola Taylor had been recording as a solo artist for RPM records, though with limited success. She had a "good sound" on these recordings. "Taylor had been recording as a solo artist with little success, but she had a good sound on her recordings for RPM records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Victim of Lymon's Addiction
podcast.body: Frankie Lymon, who became Zola Taylor's second husband, reportedly stole from her regularly to support his heroin addiction. "Lyman would apparently regularly steal from Zola Taylor, who became his second wife, to feed his heroin addiction."
